6544231356.title: [Bug bounty] getRouterFees drops the sending leg destination fee when the swap destination is the exchange chain (re-report of #2592, origin-only half)
6544231356.description:
> Note: this is a re-report of #2592, which was closed for not following the bug bounty template. The bug itself was not evaluated. This report follows the template and reproduces the bug live through the public XCM API. It covers only the origin-only half of #2592. The destination-only half (receiving leg origin fee) is deliberately NOT re-reported here: it duplicates #2171, which is already confirmed, paid and reserved.

# Bug Report

## Describe the Bug

`getRouterFees` (`packages/swap/src/transfer/getRouterFees.ts`) drops the sending leg destination fee in a one-leg routed swap where the destination is the exchange chain. In the three-leg path the swap is only added to `mergedHops` when both legs exist:

```ts
...(sendingChain && receivingChain
  ? [{ chain: exchange.chain,
       result: { ...swapChain,
                 fee: swapChain.fee + (receivingChain?.origin.fee ?? 0n),
                 isExchange: true } }]
  : []),
```

When only the sending leg exists (destination is the exchange chain), there is no exchange hop, `finalOrigin` is the sending leg origin, `finalDestination` is the swap fee, and `hops` are the sending leg hops only — so `sendingChain.destination.fee` is in no segment. It is a real fee the user pays: it is the fee for executing the incoming XCM leg on the exchange chain. The both-legs branch proves the fee must be counted: it folds the receiving leg origin fee into the exchange hop the same way.

The same omission exists in `getSwapInfo.ts`: its exchange hop entry is also built only when `sendingInfo && receivingInfo`, and its `finalOrigin` is `sendingInfo.origin`, so `sendingInfo.destination` is dropped there too.

## To Reproduce

Two read-only calls to the public XCM API. No transaction is submitted and nothing is signed. Sender `5DdcCSE2VwY6P6fDVfCN9FAvABv2ka417GiWnYUpe9ZcNE5D` is a real public account with vDOT on Hydration (free 33,162,071,409). The currency is vDOT on Hydration (asset id 15, decimals 10), so amount `0.1` is 0.1 vDOT.

1. Routed swap fee quote (origin-only: destination is the exchange chain):

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.paraspell.xyz/v2/xcm-fee" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"Hydration","to":"BifrostPolkadot",
       "currency":{"id":"15","amount":"0.1"},
       "sender":"5DdcCSE2VwY6P6fDVfCN9FAvABv2ka417GiWnYUpe9ZcNE5D",
       "recipient":"5DdcCSE2VwY6P6fDVfCN9FAvABv2ka417GiWnYUpe9ZcNE5D",
       "swapOptions":{"currencyTo":{"symbol":"DOT"},
                      "exchange":"BifrostPolkadot"}}'
```

Observed result (run 2026-11-22 ~14:15 UTC):

```json

  "origin": { "fee": "173", "asset": { "symbol": "USDT", "assetId": "10" } },
  "destination": { "fee": "82896709668", "isExchange": true,
                   "asset": { "symbol": "BNC" } },
  "hops": [] }
```

```bash

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"Hydration","to":"BifrostPolkadot",

6544217156.title: [Bug bounty] buildOriginInfo reports native fee asset as sufficient below existential deposit (re-report of #2593)
6544217156.description:
> Note: this is a re-report of #2593, which was closed for not following the bug bounty template. The bug itself was not evaluated. This report follows the template and reproduces the bug live through the public XCM API. One claim from the closed report is corrected here: `selectedCurrency.sufficient` is not false in the dust case (it does not subtract the fee, and its balanceAfter stays above the ED); the wrong flag is `xcmFee.sufficient`, which is true while its own `balanceAfter` is below the ED.

# Bug Report

## Describe the Bug

`buildOriginInfo` (`packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/transfer-info/buildOriginInfo.ts`) reports the origin XCM fee as sufficient when the remaining native fee-asset balance is below the existential deposit.

```ts
const remaining = originBalanceFeeAfter + (isNativeFeeAsset ? ed : 0n)
sufficient: transferredFeeAsset
  ? remaining === 0n || remaining >= ed
  : originBalanceFee >= originFee
```

For a native fee asset, adding the existential deposit before comparing against the existential deposit shifts the check: `remaining >= ed` is equivalent to `balanceAfter >= 0`, so any non-negative remainder passes, including dust below the ED. A remainder of exactly `-ED` also passes, because `remaining` becomes `0`. The correct check on the balance after the transfer is `balanceAfter === 0n || balanceAfter >= ed` — the same rule the sibling `selectedCurrency` check already applies (`balanceAfter >= BigInt(asset.existentialDeposit)`).

## To Reproduce

Two read-only calls to the public XCM API. No transaction is submitted and nothing is signed. The sender is my own address, `1HPCqzjFY3a8Kx2dZS6rvmeMqpJ68GTbnchwqpbVizWAN6g`, on AssetHubPolkadot; the destination is Hydration; the currency is native DOT (decimals 10, AssetHubPolkadot native ED 100,000,000 planck = 0.01 DOT).

1. Probe call with a small amount, to learn the fee and the balance from the response:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.paraspell.xyz/v2/transfer-info" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"AssetHubPolkadot","to":"Hydration",
       "currency":{"symbol":{"type":"Native","value":"DOT"},"amount":"0.1"},
       "sender":"1HPCqzjFY3a8Kx2dZS6rvmeMqpJ68GTbnchwqpbVizWAN6g",
       "recipient":"1HPCqzjFY3a8Kx2dZS6rvmeMqpJ68GTbnchwqpbVizWAN6g"}'
```

Observed (run 2026-11-22 ~14:13 UTC): `origin.xcmFee.fee` 315,298,577, `origin.xcmFee.balance` 15,913,570,677.

2. Main call. Derive the amount from the probe response's own numbers so the remainder lands below the ED:

`amount = balance - fee - 50,000,000`
`= 15,913,570,677 - 315,298,577 - 50,000,000`
`= 15,548,272,100 planck = 1.55482721 DOT`

Note: the API takes `amount` in decimal DOT, not planck — passing `"1000000000"` would be read as 1,000,000,000 DOT.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.paraspell.xyz/v2/transfer-info" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"AssetHubPolkadot","to":"Hydration",
       "currency":{"symbol":{"type":"Native","value":"DOT"},"amount":"1.55482721"},
       "sender":"1HPCqzjFY3a8Kx2dZS6rvmeMqpJ68GTbnchwqpbVizWAN6g",
       "recipient":"1HPCqzjFY3a8Kx2dZS6rvmeMqpJ68GTbnchwqpbVizWAN6g"}'
```

Observed result (run 2026-11-22 ~14:14 UTC):

```json
{ "origin": {
    "selectedCurrency": { "sufficient": true, "balance": "15913570677",
                          "balanceAfter": "365298577" },
    "xcmFee": { "sufficient": true, "fee": "315598577",
                "balance": "15913570677", "balanceAfter": "49700000",
                "asset": { "symbol": "DOT",
                           "existentialDeposit": "100000000" } } } }
```

The fee moved slightly between the probe and the main call (315,298,577 -> 315,598,577), so `balanceAfter` landed at 49,700,000 instead of exactly 50,000,000 — still below the 100,000,000 ED.

Expected: `origin.xcmFee.sufficient` is `false`, because `balanceAfter` 49,700,000 is below the existential deposit 100,000,000.
Actual: `origin.xcmFee.sufficient` is `true`.

6544204906.title: [Bug bounty] computeAllFees uses destination fee without checking its asset, native-denominated fee spent as fee-asset units (re-report of #2607)
6544204906.description:
> Note: this is a re-report of #2607, which was closed for not following the bug bounty template. The bug itself was not evaluated. This report follows the template and reproduces the bug live against the chains through the public Builder interface.

# Bug Report

## Describe the Bug

`computeAllFees` uses the destination fee without checking which asset it is denominated in, so a native-denominated fee is spent as units of the fee asset.

In `packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/type-and-then/computeFees.ts`, `sumHopFees` filters hop fees by asset equality (lines 25-30), but `destFee = result.destination.fee` (line 71) has no asset check at all. `createTypeAndThenCall` then funds `BuyExecution` with `hopFees + destFee` in fee-asset units (`packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/type-and-then/createCustomXcm.ts`).

In the `getXcmFeeOnce` fallback branches (`packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/fees/getXcmFeeOnce.ts`, around lines 86-124 and 281-289), the destination fee is native-denominated and its asset is forced to the destination native asset (`asset: api.findNativeAssetInfoOrThrow(destination)`). Those branches run when the origin dry run fails or the origin fee type is `paymentInfo`. `computeAllFees` then treats that native-denominated number as if it were denominated in the fee asset.

## To Reproduce

Prerequisite: a sender on AssetHubPolkadot that holds USDT (asset id 1984) but no DOT, so the origin dry run fails. The sender below is a real public account, verified on-chain on 2026-11-22 (USDT (id 1984) 1,000,510, DOT free 0). No transaction is submitted and nothing is signed; this is read-only fee estimation and transaction construction.

```ts
import { Builder } from '@paraspell/sdk-pjs' // version 14.5.3
import { Native } from '@paraspell/assets'

const fee = await Builder()
  .from('AssetHubPolkadot')
  .to('Hydration')
  .currency({ symbol: Native('DOT'), amount: 10000000000n }) // 1 DOT
  .feeAsset({ id: '1984' }) // USDT on AssetHub
  .sender('135xCmWABfu3LSo9b1xSjcx27GdMHD2UbomYDSFVY4rQbBrt')
  .recipient('5DdcCSE2VwY6P6fDVfCN9FAvABv2ka417GiWnYUpe9ZcNE5D')
  .getXcmFee()

const tx = await Builder()
  .from('AssetHubPolkadot')
  .to('Hydration')
  .currency({ symbol: Native('DOT'), amount: 10000000000n }) // 1 DOT
  .feeAsset({ id: '1984' }) // USDT on AssetHub
  .sender('135xCmWABfu3LSo9b1xSjcx27GdMHD2UbomYDSFVY4rQbBrt')
  .recipient('5DdcCSE2VwY6P6fDVfCN9FAvABv2ka417GiWnYUpe9ZcNE5D')
  .build()
```

**Observed result (run 2026-11-22, AssetHubPolkadot specVersion 2005003, Hydration specVersion 458):** `getXcmFee()` returns `success: false`. The origin dry run fails with `LocalExecutionIncompleteWithError / FailedToTransactAsset` at instruction 0 (the sender holds no DOT), and the destination comes back as `{ fee: "15193966112520", feeType: "paymentInfo", asset: HDX (native of Hydration, 12 decimals) }` — a native-denominated fee, not the fee asset USDT.

`build()` succeeds and returns a `polkadotXcm.execute` whose `BuyExecution` spends **1,128,000,626 units of USDT** (location `PalletInstance: 50, GeneralIndex: 1984`) — that is 1,128 USDT. The nested destination-leg `BuyExecution` in the same message is only 604 units of USDT.

Expected: the built transaction funds the destination execution with a fee denominated in USDT, of the same order as the 432 USDT units the SDK quotes for the destination fee when the origin dry run succeeds (see control below).
Actual: it funds `BuyExecution` with 1,128,000,626 USDT units — a native-denominated number spent as USDT units, about 2.6 million times the correctly priced destination fee.

6544184366.title: [Bug bounty] validateTransact returns ValidationError instead of throwing, sender check is dead (re-report of #2594)
6544184366.description:
> Note: this is a re-report of #2594, which was closed for not following the bug bounty template. The bug itself was not evaluated. This report follows the template and reproduces the bug live through the public Builder interface.

# Bug Report

## Describe the Bug

`validateTransact` returns a `ValidationError` instead of throwing it, so its sender check never runs. The last check in the function is the only one written as a `return`:

File: `packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/utils/validationUtils.ts`

```ts
if (typeof address === 'string' && sender && !compareAddresses(api, address, sender)) {
  return new ValidationError(
    'Sender address must match the destination address for transact to work.'
  )
}
```

Every other check in the same function throws (`UnsupportedOperationError`, `ValidationError` for a non-hex call). The caller ignores the return value:

File: `packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/createTransfer.ts`

```ts
validateDestination(origin, destination, api)
validateTransact(options) // return value ignored
```

So a transact transfer whose recipient differs from its sender passes validation and is built, even though the SDK's own rule says the sender must match the destination address for transact to work.

## To Reproduce

```ts
import { ApiPromise, HttpProvider } from '@polkadot/api'
import { Builder } from '@paraspell/sdk-pjs' // version 14.5.3

const hydApi = await ApiPromise.create({ provider: new HttpProvider('https://rpc.hydradx.cloud') })
const ahApi = await ApiPromise.create({ provider: new HttpProvider('https://polkadot-asset-hub-rpc.polkadot.io') })

// system.remark('paraspell-2594-repro') built on AssetHubPolkadot
const callHex = '0x6004000050706172617370656c6c2d323539342d726570726f'

const tx = await Builder({ apiOverrides: { Hydration: hydApi, AssetHubPolkadot: ahApi } })
  .from('Hydration')
  .to('AssetHubPolkadot')
  .currency({ id: '10', amount: 100000000n }) // 100 USDT (id 10)
  .sender('5DdcCSE2VwY6P6fDVfCN9FAvABv2ka417GiWnYUpe9ZcNE5D')
  .recipient('1HPCqzjFY3a8Kx2dZS6rvmeMqpJ68GTbnchwqpbVizWAN6g') // a different address
  .transact(callHex)
  .build()
```

No transaction is submitted and nothing is signed; `.build()` only builds the extrinsic.

**Observed result (run 2026-11-22, Node.js v24.22.1, Linux, `@paraspell/sdk-pjs` 14.5.3, Hydration specVersion 458, AssetHubPolkadot specVersion 2005003):** `.build()` SUCCEEDED and returned a `polkadotXcm` execute extrinsic (callIndex `0x6b03`). `.getXcmFee()` on the same mismatched transfer also returned a result instead of throwing (`origin.fee: 408`). Control with sender equal to recipient returned the same fee (`origin.fee: 408`): the mismatch changes nothing, the check is dead.

Two notes on the exact values: the currency must be `{ id: '10' }`, not `{ symbol: 'USDT' }` — the symbol is ambiguous on Hydration and the SDK throws `DuplicateAssetError` before reaching the bug (aliases USDT1 id 10, USDT2 id 1000767, USDT3 id 23). An earlier run with currency HDX hit an unrelated chain rejection (`DryRunFailedError`, Hydration rejects the HDX teleport to AssetHubPolkadot, `UntrustedTeleportLocation` at instruction 2) in both the mismatched and the control run; the USDT route above avoids it and isolates the validation bug.

## Environment

- OS: Linux
- Framework: Node.js v24.22.1
- XCM Tool version: @paraspell/sdk-pjs 14.5.3
- NodeJS version: v24.22.1

## Screenshots / Logs

Live run output, 2026-11-22 (read-only, no transaction submitted, nothing signed):

```
MAIN getXcmFee, sender != recipient ...
MAIN getXcmFee RESULT: returned (no ValidationError). success: false origin.fee: 408
MAIN build, sender != recipient ...
MAIN build RESULT: SUCCEEDED. method: {"callIndex":"0x6b03","args":{"message":{"v5":[{"withdrawAsset":...
CONTROL getXcmFee, sender == recipient ...
CONTROL getXcmFee RESULT: success: false origin.fee: 408
```

## Expected Behavior

`.build()` (and `.getXcmFee()`) throws `ValidationError: Sender address must match the destination address for transact to work.` when the recipient differs from the sender on a transact transfer, the same way the other checks in `validateTransact` throw.

## Additional Context

Suggested fix (one word, in `validationUtils.ts`):

```ts
if (typeof address === 'string' && sender && !compareAddresses(api, address, sender)) {
  throw new ValidationError(
    'Sender address must match the destination address for transact to work.'
  )
}
```

The check exists because the destination chain executes the transact call under the sender's account; building the transfer with a different recipient silently produces an extrinsic the SDK itself considers invalid, which the user can then submit. The repo's own test codifies the bug: `packages/sdk-core/src/transfer/utils/validationUtils.test.ts:452`, "returns ValidationError if sender does not match destination", asserts the return value instead of a throw. Previous report: #2594 (closed for template non-compliance, bug not evaluated).

---

6544172615.title: [Bug bounty] findEthAssetBySymbol silently picks the first of two distinct XRT contracts on Ethereum instead of throwing a duplicate error (re-report of #2613)
6544172615.description:
> Note: this is a re-report of #2613, which was closed for not following the bug bounty template. The bug itself was not evaluated. This report follows the template and reproduces the bug live through the documented public function `findAssetInfo`.

# Bug Report

## Describe the Bug

Ethereum has two different XRT tokens registered in `packages/assets/src/maps/assets.json`, two distinct contracts:

- `0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7` (alias XRT2)
- `0x1f752250f518e419f2f03804e25728c5c6dff73f` (alias XRT1)

Every other symbol path in `packages/assets/src/assets/search/findAssetInfoBySymbol.ts` guards against this: when more than one asset matches a symbol it throws `DuplicateAssetError` and tells the caller to use the `ForeignAbstract()` selector with the alias. The Ethereum-specific path does not. `findEthAssetBySymbol` filters the assets to the Ethereum GlobalConsensus entries and returns `findBestMatches(...)[0]` with no duplicate check, and `findEthMatch` returns that result directly. That path is taken whenever the destination is an external chain (Ethereum) or the symbol ends with `.e` — exactly the lookups used for transfers to Ethereum and for Snowbridge assets.

## To Reproduce

```ts
import { findAssetInfo, getAssetsObject } from '@paraspell/sdk' // version 14.5.3

// The registry really has two distinct XRT contracts on Ethereum:
getAssetsObject('Ethereum').assets
  .filter(a => a.symbol === 'XRT')
  .map(a => ({ assetId: a.assetId, alias: a.alias }))
// => [{ assetId: '0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7', alias: 'XRT2' },
//     { assetId: '0x1f752250f518e419f2f03804e25728c5c6dff73f', alias: 'XRT1' }]

// Destination is Ethereum: silently returns the first contract
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', { symbol: 'XRT' }, 'Ethereum')

// Snowbridge '.e' symbol: silently returns the first contract
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', { symbol: 'XRT.e' })
```

**Observed result (run 2026-11-22, `@paraspell/sdk` 14.5.3, Node.js v24.22.1):** both calls return the same asset with no error and no warning:

```json
{ "symbol": "XRT",
  "assetId": "0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7",
  "decimals": 9, "existentialDeposit": "1",
  "location": { "parents": 2, "interior": { "X2": [
    { "GlobalConsensus": { "Ethereum": { "chainId": 1 } } },
    { "AccountKey20": { "network": null,
      "key": "0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7" } } ] } },
  "alias": "XRT2" }
```

The second contract (`0x1f752250f518e419f2f03804e25728c5c6dff73f`, alias XRT1) is never surfaced.

Control — the plain symbol path on the same chain, same symbol, throws as it should:

```
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', { symbol: 'XRT' })
=> THROWS: DuplicateAssetError: Multiple foreign assets found for symbol XRT. Please specify with ForeignAbstract() selector. Available aliases: XRT2 (ID:0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7), XRT1 (ID:0x1f752250f518e419f2f03804e25728c5c6dff73f)
```

So the codebase already knows this symbol is ambiguous and already has the guard and the disambiguation mechanism (the XRT1/XRT2 aliases) — the Ethereum path just skips the guard.

## Environment

- OS: Linux
- Framework: Node.js v24.22.1
- XCM Tool version: @paraspell/sdk 14.5.3
- NodeJS version: v24.22.1

## Screenshots / Logs

Live run output, 2026-11-22 (registry lookup only, no chain connection, no transaction):

```
Ethereum XRT entries: [{"assetId":"0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7","alias":"XRT2"},{"assetId":"0x1f752250f518e419f2f03804e25728c5c6dff73f","alias":"XRT1"}]
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', {symbol:'XRT'}, 'Ethereum') => OK: {"symbol":"XRT","assetId":"0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7",...,"alias":"XRT2"}
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', {symbol:'XRT.e'}) => OK: {"symbol":"XRT","assetId":"0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7",...,"alias":"XRT2"}
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', {symbol:'XRT'}) [control: plain path] => THROWS: DuplicateAssetError: Multiple foreign assets found for symbol XRT. Please specify with ForeignAbstract() selector. Available aliases: XRT2 (ID:0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7), XRT1 (ID:0x1f752250f518e419f2f03804e25728c5c6dff73f)
findAssetInfo('Ethereum', {symbol:'XRT.e'}, 'Ethereum') => OK: {"symbol":"XRT","assetId":"0x7de91b204c1c737bcee6f000aaa6569cf7061cb7",...,"alias":"XRT2"}
```

## Expected Behavior

The Ethereum paths throw the same `DuplicateAssetError` as the plain symbol path, naming both aliases (XRT2 and XRT1) so the caller can disambiguate with `ForeignAbstract('XRT1')` or `ForeignAbstract('XRT2')` — instead of silently returning whichever contract happens to be listed first.

## Additional Context

Suggested fix: apply the duplicate guard in `findEthAssetBySymbol` (`packages/assets/src/assets/search/findAssetInfoBySymbol.ts:13-24`), the same `throwDuplicateAssetError` the other paths already use. This is the same class of bug as #2236 (plain-symbol `.e` lookups skipping the duplicate guard), which was confirmed.

Impact: a user moving XRT to or from Ethereum through the `.e` symbol o

analysis.explanation: Bug report on silent failure/ambiguity when encountering duplicate token contracts on Ethereum.

## Description
`payout_participant` transfers the reward, forwards a fee to `quid-fee-collector`, releases stake and calls `quid-reputation`. If a reward token or linked contract misbehaves, the order of state writes and external calls matters. Apply checks-effects-interactions and prove it with a malicious token test.

## User Story
**As a** hunter,  
**I want to** a payout to settle exactly once even if a token contract misbehaves,  
**so that** nobody can be paid twice or drain the escrow.

- Mark the submission `Paid` and update counters before any `token::Client` transfer or cross-contract call.
- The reputation call failing must not block the payout. Use `try_` client methods and emit a `ReputationHookFailed` event.
- Add a test-only hostile token contract that calls back into `payout_participant` during `transfer`, and assert the re-entry fails.

6544297472.title: feat: migrate the gq plugin from the old bastproxy
6544297472.description:
## Problem

The old bastproxy's `plugins/aardwolf/gq.py` followed Aardwolf global quests: declared and started quests, the one joined, its target mobs from `gq check`, the mobs killed, extended time, rewards, and how it ended. It has not been migrated. `statdb` (#26) records each global quest in its `gquests` table and its mobs in `gqmobs`.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `gq` plugin (`plugins.aardwolf.gq`) that keeps the old behaviour on the new APIs.

**Input:**
- A watch on `^(gq|gqu|gque|gques|gquest) (c|ch|che|chec|check)$` (core `watch` plugin) clears the mobs left and enables the `gqcheck` group.
- The triggers from the old file, copied as they are:
  - always on: declared, joined, started, cancelled, quit, the gquest forum note, and the maximum-kills line;
  - `gqcheck`: not in a gquest, a target mob line, not started yet, and the wins-left line;
  - `gqin`: a gquest mob killed, extended time, first to complete, finished, and the win announcement;
  - `gqrew`: the reward lines.

**State**, kept with `PersistentDict` in the plugin's data directory:
- `mobs`, the original target list, each with `name`, `nocolorname`, `location` and `num`;
- `trains`, `pracs`, `gold`, `tp`, `qp` (reward names map through `aardu.REWARDTABLE`), `qpmobs`;
- `level`, from `aardu.actual_level_from_gmcp`;
- `starttime`, `finishtime`, `length`;
- `won`, `completed`, `extended`.

The mobs still left are kept as well. The settings `joined` (the gquest number joined, -1 for none) and `maxkills` stay, along with the declared and started gquest numbers.

**Events** (the old names were `aard_gq_*`):

| Event | When | Data |
|---|---|---|
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_declared` | a gquest is declared | the trigger groups |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_joined` | the character joins one | the trigger groups |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_started` | a gquest starts | the trigger groups |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_cancelled` | a gquest is cancelled | `{"gqnum": n}` |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_mobsleft` | after `gq check`, and when a target mob is killed | `{"mobsleft": [...]}` |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_won` | the character won | a copy of the state |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_completed` | the character finished in extended time | a copy of the state |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_done` | the gquest ended otherwise, with gquest mobs killed | a copy of the state |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.gq_available` / `gq_notavailable` | a gquest is, or no longer is, declared | none |

Declare each with `event.add` and describe its data keys.

**Killed mobs:** when the gquest-mob line is seen, add 3 to `qpmobs` unless `maxkills` is set, take the next `ev_plugins.aardwolf.mobk_kill`, and count that mob down. If no target matches, send `gq check`.

**Old bugs to fix in the migration** (the maintainer can object in review):
1. **The kill listener:** `_mobkillevent` registers itself again instead of unregistering, so it handles every later kill. Unregister it.
2. **The first mob:** a match at index 0 is never removed (`if removeitem:`). Test for `is not None`.
3. **`joined` reset:** `_gqreset` sets the integer setting `joined` to the string `'default'`. Set it back to -1.
4. **`mobsleft` type:** `_gqnew` sets it to a dict and `_gqjoined` to a list. Use a list.
5. **Level:** `_gqnew` calls the old `getactuallevel` with the level only; use `aardu.actual_level_from_gmcp`.

**Dropped:** the `send.msg` debug echoes go to the plugin logger at debug level.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `plugins.aardwolf.gq` loads through the entry point.
- [ ] Recorded output for declare, join, start, `gq check`, target kills, extended time, a win, a finish in extended time, a quit and a cancel raises the events in the table with the listed data.
- [ ] A target kill is handled once, and the first mob in the list is counted down and removed.
- [ ] The state and settings survive a plugin reload and a proxy restart.
- [ ] Tests cover the above, with the mobk event faked. Any new test file importing `aardwolf` is added to `pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection`.
- [ ] `docs/plugins/gq.md` documents the plugin and is listed in the plugins index.
- [ ] A live check against Aardwolf: joining a gquest raises `gq_joined` and `gq_started`, and killing a target raises `gq_mobsleft`.

## Additional Context

- Old source: `~/src/bastproxy-old/plugins/aardwolf/gq.py`, 435 lines.
- It needs the mobk plugin's (#27) `mobk_kill` event; without mobk loaded, target kills are found only through the next `gq check`.
- Plugins must not import other plugins; `aardwolf.libs.aardu` is a library, so importing it is fine.
- Related: #26 (statdb), and #27 (mobk).

analysis.explanation: Clear feature request to migrate an existing proxy plugin to new APIs with well-defined inputs and state storage.

6544297182.title: feat: migrate the cp plugin from the old bastproxy
6544297182.description:
## Problem

The old bastproxy's `plugins/aardwolf/cp.py` followed Aardwolf campaigns: the target mobs from `campaign check`, the mobs killed, the rewards and the completion or failure. It has not been migrated. `statdb` (#26) records each campaign in its `campaigns` table and its mobs in `cpmobs`.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `cp` plugin (`plugins.aardwolf.cp`) that keeps the old behaviour on the new APIs.

**Input:**
- A `campaign check` command type in the core mudcmds plugin (`type.add`, `command.queue`, `command.start`, `command.finish`; the old plugin used `cmdq`). It is queued after first active, on a new campaign, and by the `refresh` command.
- The trigger groups from the old file, copied as they are:
  - `cpcheck`: new campaign, no campaign, time left, a target mob line, and the scramble line, all omitted from the client;
  - `cpin`: need to level, can take a new one, next shuffle time, mob dead, complete and cleared;
  - `cprew`: the reward lines;
  - `cpdone`: the completion summary.
- After the completion summary, read the next lines for the first-campaign-of-the-day bonus qp line or the campaigns-today count, using the core triggers' every-line support (the old plugin used `trigger_all`).

**State**, kept with `PersistentDict` in the plugin's data directory:
- `oncp`, `cantake`, `shtime`;
- `mobs`, the original target list, each with `name`, `nocolorname`, `location` and `mobdead`;
- `trains`, `pracs`, `gold`, `tp`, `qp`, `bonusqp` (reward names map through `aardu.REWARDTABLE`);
- `failed`, `starttime`, `finishtime`;
- `level`, from `aardu.actual_level_from_gmcp`.

The mobs still left are kept as well.

**Events** (the old names were `aard_cp_*`):

| Event | When | Data |
|---|---|---|
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.cp_mobsorig` | the first `campaign check` of a campaign | `{"mobsleft": [...]}` |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.cp_mobsleft` | after each `campaign check`, and when a target mob is killed | `{"mobsleft": [...]}` |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.cp_comp` | the campaign completed, after the bonus line | a copy of the state |
| `ev_plugins.aardwolf.cp_failed` | the campaign was cleared | a copy of the state with `failed=1` |

Declare each with `event.add` and describe its data keys.

**Killed mobs:** when the mob-dead line is seen, take the next `ev_plugins.aardwolf.mobk_kill` (the mobk plugin's event) and remove that mob from the mobs left. If no target matches, queue a `campaign check`.

**APIs:** `oncp` (whether a campaign is active) and `mobs.left.get` (a copy of the mobs left).

**Commands:** `show`, which lists the mobs left, and `refresh`, which queues a `campaign check`; both return `CommandResult`.

**Old bugs to fix in the migration** (the maintainer can object in review):
1. **The first mob:** `_mobkillevent` removes the matched mob only `if removeitem:`, so a match at index 0 is never removed. Test for `is not None`.
2. **Level:** `_cpreset` calls the old `getactuallevel` with the level only; use `aardu.actual_level_from_gmcp`.
3. **No bonus line:** if neither line follows the completion summary, `cp_comp` is never raised. Stop waiting at the next prompt and raise it then.

**Dropped:** the `send.msg` debug echoes go to the plugin logger at debug level.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `plugins.aardwolf.cp` loads through the entry point.
- [ ] Recorded output for a new campaign, a `campaign check`, a target kill, completion with and without the bonus line, and a cleared campaign raises the events in the table with the listed data.
- [ ] A kill of the first mob in the list removes it.
- [ ] The state survives a plugin reload and a proxy restart.
- [ ] Tests cover the above, with the mobk event faked. Any new test file importing `aardwolf` is added to `pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection`.
- [ ] `docs/plugins/cp.md` documents the plugin and is listed in the plugins index.
- [ ] A live check against Aardwolf: taking a campaign raises `cp_mobsorig`, killing a target raises `cp_mobsleft` without it, and completing raises `cp_comp`.

## Additional Context

- Old source: `~/src/bastproxy-old/plugins/aardwolf/cp.py`, 392 lines.
- It needs the mobk plugin's (#27) `mobk_kill` event; without mobk loaded, target kills are found only through the next `campaign check`.
- Plugins must not import other plugins; `aardwolf.libs.aardu` is a library, so importing it is fine.
- Related: #26 (statdb), and #27 (mobk).

6544290750.description:
**Area:** gameplay (Gameplay-Engineer builds; spec by Design-Agent, from #5645)

**Why.** Growth Nov 19: 22 to 27% of Tier 3 players never land in the Neighbourhood, and those who catch there reach Tier 4 82 to 84% of the time. Still playing goes 31% at 5 min to 19% at 10 min (Nov 21). hoodTrail already points the way; the landing has no reward the player sees at once.

**Spec.** Behind a new switch `hoodWelcome` (LiveFlags.OFF_BY_DEFAULT, first-session rule: on the hour it publishes after Review-QA).
1. At Tier 3, on the account's first Neighbourhood landing, one stray of a Neighbourhood kind the player does not own waits near the camp landing, the same way tier3Path's waiting stray works at the Park (reuse that path, do not copy it).
2. Its rarity is the area's normal roll among kinds not owned; if every Neighbourhood kind is owned, no stray is added.
3. Normal circle, normal rings, normal miss (Derek #5637: no slow one-shot circle). missKeepsCommon applies as everywhere.
4. One toast when it appears: "A new kind is nearby". No window, no arrow forced, no camera move, no teleport.
5. Once per account. Log `hood_welcome` (shown, caught) so Growth can read it against tier3_left.

**Test plan.** Spec for the pure part (who gets the stray, once per account, none when all kinds are owned). Studio: fresh save to Tier 3, fly to the Neighbourhood, the stray waits near the landing, catch it with the normal circle; switch off gives today's landing.

6544199765.title: Easter eggs: hidden discoveries from specific actions
6544199765.description:
This is an idea, not approved work. Context: `coordination/design/NOTEQUEST_FEATURE_MAP_v1.0.md` (commit `3343d04a49d7ff5b516bb87fefa3195752ec1fd7`).

Hidden discoveries a learner finds by doing a specific thing, not by opening a menu. Examples Kevin gave:

- Play a secret melody at the fountain.
- Tap the floating castle 5 times.
- A night-time village.

## What exists today

None of these triggers exist.

- The fountain and the castle in the shop (`DECOR` in `index.html`) are objects placed in a pet pen. They are not the overlook's fountain or the floating castle in the title art.
- Pets already sleep during night hours (default 8:30 pm–6:30 am). The village has no night scene.
- The floating castle is in the loading-screen concept. It is not a tappable object in the running game.

## Constraints

- An egg is a reward for looking. It is not a second curriculum and not a coin trick. Finding one should feel like a secret, and missing it must not block a lesson, a world, or a pet.
- The learning path stays obvious. Eggs must not be the only way to reach a practice tool.
- Building assignments in the overlook are not decided. Do not hard-wire an egg to "the fountain building" until Kevin assigns buildings. Action triggers (a melody, a count of taps, the clock) can be designed before that assignment.
- Night-time should respect the sleep hours a grown-up can change, and it should have a reduced-motion path like the rest of the overlook.

## Open questions

- Are eggs per learner, and do they stay found?
- Does the secret melody have to be played on the real piano, or on the on-screen keys?
- Is the night village a palette change of the overlook, or a separate visit?

Filed by Coding Agent (Grok) for Kevin
